title: Last Aiders in the Workplace: Development, Evaluation, and Implementation
summary:
Serious illness, dying, death and grief can also play an important role in working life. Employees may become seriously ill themselves, care for or lose relatives, or be affected by the illness or death of colleagues. At the same time, many workplaces lack appropriate support services and designated contact persons.

The aim of LAUT 2.0 is to develop and pilot a training module specifically designed for Last Aiders in the Workplace. Last Aiders in the Workplace are intended to support employees with questions and difficult situations related to serious illness, dying, death and grief and, where appropriate, refer them to further support services.

The study will investigate how participants evaluate the training module, how already trained Last Aiders in the Workplace perform their role in everyday working life, and which conditions facilitate or hinder the sustainable implementation and use of this role in organizations. Online questionnaires, focus groups and individual interviews will be conducted.
conditions: Serious illness, dying, death and grief in the workplace

interventions.name: Participants in the three sub-studies of LAUT 2.0: pilot testing and evaluation of the advanced training module for Last Aiders in the Workplace, evaluation of the role of already trained Last Aiders in the Workplace, and investigation of the conditions for sustainable implementation. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Depending on the sub-study: (P1) employees participating in the training module “Last Aider in the Workplace” who consent to the scientific evaluation; (P2) persons who have successfully completed the training module and have had sufficient opportunity to perform the role as a Last Aider in the Workplace; (P3) Last Aiders in the Workplace, managers and other workplace stakeholders involved in the introduction, implementation or sustainable integration of the role. Voluntary informed consent to the respective study procedure is required.
Exclusion criteria:
Depending on the sub-study: no participation in the training module or no consent to the evaluation (P1); no completion of the training module, insufficient opportunity to perform the role, or no consent (P2); no relevant involvement in the introduction, implementation or sustainable integration of the role, or no consent (P3).
